8.text: Among the Asiatic Eskimo, transformed persons are found even now, as

9.text: may be seen from what was told² about Čaivuˊurg̣ɪn of Indian Point.

10.text: Mr. Gondatti asserts in his paper on the Population of the Anadyr District³ (and

11.text: also in a verbal communication), that at Indian Point the transformed shamans

12.text: have a great and baleful influence, which he, on his arrival, tried to counteract,

13.text: and succeeded in partly overcoming. Mr. Gondatti was the chief official of

14.text: the Anadyr country, and the curtailment of the unhealthy influence of the

15.text: shamans lay evidently within the province of his duties (of course, from a

16.text: Russian official point of view). When, however, I visited Indian Point, the

17.text: only transformed person I found there was the sickly Čaivuˊurg̣ɪn. Another

18.text: “soft man,” of greater age, whom Mr. Gondatti had probably met, died

19.text: from measles in 1900. Other inhabitants did not undertake to follow his

20.text: practices, remembering, perhaps, the reproofs of Mr. Gondatti.

21.text: SHAMANISTIC GARMENTS. — The shamanism of the Chukchee has not

22.text: reached a stage of development high enough to have drums or clothing of

23.text: peculiar form, or, indeed, any special belongings characteristic of itself. The

24.text: Chukchee shaman uses the ordinary drum of his family, or perhaps he may

25.text: make an extra drum for his own use; but this drum will have exactly the

26.text: same form, and, moreover, it will probably be employed in all the family

27.text: ceremonials, where additional drums are used for making as much noise as

29.text: As to the shamanistic garb, the Chukchee have nothing similar to the

30.text: well-known type of coat covered with fringes and images, which is in general

31.text: use among the Yakut and Tungus, and which probably was borrowed from

32.text: the latter by the Yukaghir, and perhaps also by the Kamchadal, if we may

33.text: judge by the representations in Steller’s book.⁴ To understand the reasons

34.text: for the absence of a peculiar shaman’s dress among the Chukchee, we must

35.text: remember that their shamans perform most of their practices in the inner

36.text: room of the house, in total darkness, where the outer appearance of the

37.text: shaman is of no consequence. The atmosphere, too, is so close, that the
